steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Introduction: name the production, company, venue, date and the production's overall intention.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: SEE framework: State the technique, Evidence from the production, Effect on the audience — use for every analytical point.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Analysis paragraphs: focus on one aspect per paragraph (e.g. performance, then design, then direction).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Conclusion: evaluate the overall effectiveness — did the production achieve its intention? Sum up your judgement.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the structure of a theatre review for the GCSE written exam. | What is the SEE framework and how does it improve your written analysis? | How can you ensure your theatre review is analytical rather than just descriptive?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Introduction (production, company, venue, intention) → Performance analysis paragraph (specific vocal/physical choices) → Design analysis paragraph (specific set/lighting/sound/costume choices) → Dire | SEE: State the technique used, Evidence from the production (specific moment), Effect on the audience. It improves analysis by forcing you to move beyond description ('the lighting was blue') to analy | Use precise terminology instead of everyday language. Always explain the MEANING and EFFECT of choices, not just what you saw. Make judgements about effectiveness. Support every claim with evidence. R

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Introduction: name production, company, venue, date — essential facts first Every paragraph must contain both ANALYSIS and EVALUATION Use SEE for every point — State, Evidence, Effect Conclusion: judge overall effectiveness against the production's stated intention
